content: 1. A glossary of terms related to diabetes is a comprehensive list that explains various terms associated with the condition. 2. 3. Acetohexamide is an oral medication used to reduce blood glucose levels, often prescribed for individuals with Type 2 diabetes. It belongs to the sulfonylurea class of drugs and is also known by brand names such as Dymelor™. 4. Acetone is a byproduct of fat metabolism and one of the three ketone bodies. It can accumulate to high levels during stress, infection, or other conditions, potentially leading to diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a serious medical condition. Acetone may sometimes be detected on the breath of individuals in or approaching DKA, producing a fruity or nail polish remover-like odor. 5. Acidosis refers to an acidic state in body fluids, particularly the blood. Prolonged or severe acidosis can result in coma or death. In diabetes, it can occur due to insufficient glucose absorption (e.g., from inadequate insulin) combined with metabolic ketosis, potentially leading to diabetic ketoacidosis. 6. Acute conditions are those that occur suddenly, last for a limited time, and are often severe in nature. 7. The adrenal glands are endocrine glands located on top of the kidneys. They secrete adrenaline, a key fight or flight stress hormone with counter-regulatory effects on insulin. 8. Adult-onset diabetes is an older term for Type 2 diabetes mellitus. 9. Adverse effects are harmful outcomes or side effects resulting from a treatment or medication. 10. Albuminuria refers to the presence of the protein albumin in the urine, which is a sign of abnormal kidney function. 11. Alpha cells are a type of cell in the pancreas, specifically in the islets of Langerhans, that produce and release glucagon, a hormone that raises blood glucose levels. 12. Amino acids are organic compounds containing carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen. They are the building blocks of proteins, with about 20 types used in the human body. Roughly half of these can be synthesized internally, while the rest, known as essential amino acids, must be obtained through the diet. 13. Amyotrophy is a form of diabetic neuropathy that leads to muscle weakness and wasting. 14. Angiopathy refers to damage to blood vessels, which can occur as a complication of diabetes. 15. Anomalies are birth defects or abnormalities present at birth. 16. Antibodies are specialized proteins produced by the immune system that specifically target and attach to foreign substances, such as viruses or bacteria. In Type 1 diabetes, inappropriate antibody reactions against beta cells are thought to be a primary mechanism of beta cell destruction. 17. Antidiabetic agents are medications that help individuals with diabetes manage their blood glucose levels to maintain normal body function. Examples include insulin and oral hypoglycemic agents. 18. Antigens are substances in foreign bodies that trigger the production of specific antibodies. 19. Antiseptics are products that reduce the presence of infectious agents. 20. Arteriosclerosis, also known as atherosclerosis, refers to the hardening of blood vessels. 21. Arteries are blood vessels with muscular walls that carry blood away from the heart to the rest of the body. 22. Researchers are working on developing smaller, implantable versions of this device. 23. Aspartame is an artificial sweetener made from two amino acids. It interacts with taste buds to produce a sweet sensation. 24. Asymptomatic conditions are those without noticeable symptoms. Many individuals with Type 2 diabetes remain asymptomatic for years before diagnosis. 25. Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own tissues. Examples include Type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis, lupus, and certain forms of rheumatism. 26. Autonomic neuropathy involves damage to nerves that control involuntary bodily functions, such as heart rate and body temperature. This type of nerve damage can result in systemic effects rather than localized pain or muscle weakness. 27. Background retinopathy, also known as non-proliferative retinopathy, is an early stage of diabetic eye disease. 28. Basal rate refers to a continuous supply of a substance, such as the low levels of insulin required for basic cellular functions like amino acid and potassium uptake. 29. Beta cells, located in the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, are responsible for producing and releasing insulin in response to blood glucose levels. 30. Biosynthetic human insulin is a man-made insulin that is chemically identical to natural human insulin. 31. Biphasic insulin is a mixture of intermediate-acting and fast-acting insulin. 32. Blood glucose, or blood sugar, is the primary energy source for body cells. It is absorbed from food, stored in the liver as glycogen, and can be synthesized during starvation from triglycerides and certain amino acids. 33. 34. Blood glucose monitoring involves tracking blood glucose levels, typically using a blood glucose meter. 35. systolic (during heart contraction) and diastolic (just before the next contraction). 36. Elevated BUN levels may indicate early kidney damage. 37. Blood vessels are tubular structures that transport blood throughout the body. They include arteries, veins, and capillaries. 38. A bolus is a single, concentrated dose of a substance, such as an extra dose of insulin to manage a rise in blood glucose after a meal. 39. Brittle diabetes refers to a form of diabetes characterized by frequent and unpredictable swings in blood glucose levels. 40. Properly fitting shoes can help prevent their formation. 41. In diabetes, only calories from substances that the body can metabolize are relevant. 42. Capillaries are tiny blood vessels where gas exchange occurs, such as oxygen delivery to tissues and carbon dioxide removal. 43. Cataracts involve clouding of the lens in the eye, often associated with aging or diabetes. 44. Cerebrovascular disease refers to damage to blood vessels in the brain, which can lead to strokes. People with diabetes are at higher risk for this condition. 45. Charcot foot is a complication of diabetic neuropathy that results in joint and soft tissue destruction in the foot. 46. Chronic conditions persist over a long period, such as diabetes. 47. Clinical trials are research studies conducted in humans to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of new treatments or interventions. 48. Coma refers to a state of unconsciousness. In diabetes, it can result from severe hypoglycemia, hyperglycemia, or diabetic ketoacidosis. 49. Complications of diabetes include acute effects like hypoglycemia and long-term damage to the eyes, kidneys, blood vessels, and nerves. 50. Congenital defects are abnormalities present at birth. 51. Congestive heart failure occurs when the heart loses its ability to pump effectively, leading to fluid accumulation in the body. 52. Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) refers to the use of an insulin pump to deliver insulin continuously. 53. Dawn phenomenon is a rise in blood glucose levels in the early morning, unrelated to insulin reactions. 54. Dehydration involves a loss of body fluids, often leading to abnormal concentrations of substances in the blood. 55. Delta cells in the pancreas produce somatostatin, a hormone that regulates insulin and glucagon production. 56. Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a life-threatening condition caused by high levels of ketones and acidosis in the blood. 57. Diabetic retinopathy involves damage to the retina due to the growth of abnormal blood vessels, which can lead to blindness. 58. Dysglycemia refers to any abnormal blood glucose level, including prediabetes and diabetes. 59. Edema is the accumulation of fluid in body tissues, often seen in the feet of individuals with diabetes due to poor circulation. 60. Endocrine glands secrete hormones that regulate various bodily functions, such as insulin production by the pancreas. 61. End-stage renal disease (ESRD) is the final stage of kidney disease, often requiring dialysis or kidney transplantation. 62. Enzymes are proteins that accelerate specific chemical reactions without being consumed in the process. 63. Euglycemia refers to normal blood glucose levels. 64.
